Issued at 338 PM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

Now through Saturday Night...

It's a cold and dreary afternoon across central Kentucky and 
southern Indiana as the western edge of a robust low pressure system 
the has impacted the eastern CONUS continues to linger over the 
area. Scattered pockets of rain/drizzle are still moving through the 
region, along with blustery winds that are producing 20-25 mph wind 
gusts. Widespread lower cloud cover has also greatly restricted 
rises in temperatures, with most places in the upper 30s/low 40s. 

Conditions will begin to improve this evening as chances for rain 
and higher wind gusts quickly drop off. Broad cloud cover will still 
remain into Saturday, though much calmer weather will settle in by 
Saturday morning. For the day on Saturday, clearing skies and 5-10 
mph southerly winds will result in a milder day, with highs in the 
low to mid 50s. Cloud cover will begin to increase Saturday night 
ahead of our next system arriving on Sunday, though dry conditions 
are expected to prevail through the overnight, with lows in the 
upper 30s/low 40s.

Sunday through Sunday Night...

Our next chance for rainfall returns on Sunday as a shortwave trough 
axis and accompanying surface low passes through the region. The 
shortwave will shift from the central Plains towards the Ohio Valley 
Saturday night, with the accompanying surface low deepening as the 
trough axis transitions from a positive to a negative tilt by late 
Sunday. A jet streak will develop on the right side of the trough 
axis, also aiding in the deepening of the surface low. 

Chances for widespread showers and some isolated thunderstorms will 
increase close to daybreak on Sunday, lasting into the evening 
hours. A decent pressure gradient thanks to the deepening surface 
low will promote gusty winds for most of the day ahead of the 
accompanying cold front passing through. Sustained winds are 
currently forecast in the 15-20 mph range, with gusts around 30-35 
mph. The latest REFS 90th percentile wind gusts go as high as 45 
mph, and with a strong LLJ in place that will produce similar winds, 
that high-end range cannot be completely ruled out. The limiting 
factor to 40+ mph gusts being realized will be the meager low-level 
lapse rates that could prevent the strongest winds from mixing down. 

While a few thunderstorms could develop ahead of the cold front 
passing through, limited instability (<300 J/kg of MLCAPE) and the 
previously mentioned meager lapse rates should strongly limit the 
potential for strong to severe storms. The gusty gradient winds 
continues to be the primary focus, and if confidence in the gusts 
increases, a Wind Advisory may be needed in a future forecast 
package. Gusty winds in the 25-35 mph range could continue in the 
hours following the cold front moving through the region due to 
rapid pressure rises behind the low, extending the period of 
blustery conditions into the overnight hours on Sunday night. Cold 
air will also fill in behind the front, and if enough wrap-around 
moisture sticks around the region, a brief rain to snow transition 
could occur near the Bluegrass late Sunday night.

Monday through Friday...

As surface high pressure builds in behind the low, this active 
stretch of weather will give way to dry conditions that will last 
through at least the first half of the workweek. While temperatures 
on Monday will be on the cooler side (highs in the low to mid 40s), 
the slow eastward shift of the surface high will allow southerly 
flow to return and promote warmer temperatures each passing day. 
Afternoon highs will be close to normal on Tuesday (low to mid 50s), 
with well-above average temperatures in the mid to upper 60s 
forecast by late week.

A broad upper-level trough over the western CONUS by midweek moves 
eastward towards the region, with its accompanying surface low and 
cold front entering the Ohio Valley by late Thursday into early 
Friday. Chances for showers and thunderstorms return with this 
system, resulting in an unsettled end to next week.
